rules.quote: Cite an authorised law report if one is available
rules.violation_condition: A case citation relies on an unauthorised report or an unreported judgment instead of an available authorised report of the same decision.
when: An authorised report of the cited decision is available.
An unauthorised report may be used when no authorised report is available.
rules.why: G-2 keeps availability and the unauthorised-report fallback within one source-selection rule; G-4 absorbs the body restatement.

covers.quote: Citations use common abbreviations for the titles of law reports.
Wherever you can, cite an authorised law report using the relevant abbreviation.
Use common abbreviations for authorised reports
State and territory reports have common abbreviations for series titles that cover different periods.
ALD (Administrative Law Decisions) – Administrative Appeals Tribunal – 1976 onward
CLR (Commonwealth Law Reports) – High Court – 1903 onward
FCR (Federal Court Reports) – Federal Court – 1984 onward
IR (Industrial Reports) – Australian Industrial Relations Commission, Fair Work Australia, Fair Work Commission – 2006 onward
ACTLR (Australian Capital Territory Law Reports) – 2007 onward
NSWLR (New South Wales Law Reports) – 1971 onward
St R Qd (State Reports Queensland) – 1902 to 1957
Use standard abbreviations for unauthorised reports
If the law report has no authorised version, you might need to use the abbreviations from this select list of unauthorised law report series:

rules.quote: Use the correct abbreviations for Australian law report series.
rules.violation_condition: An Australian law-report series title in a case citation is written out instead of abbreviated, or is represented by an abbreviation that does not match that series.
when: The text names an Australian law-report series in a case citation.
The abbreviation must match the relevant series; historical state and territory series have different titles and reporting periods.
The unauthorised-series list is selective, not exhaustive.
rules.why: G-2 treats authorised and unauthorised series as cases of the same abbreviation check; G-4 consolidates the headings and restatements, with the lists supplying lookup data rather than separate rules.
